body: I think false as the default setting is fine. However, I just realized that there is a bug in the original behavior. So when reset is performed with `Abort on Reset = false`, I think the `shot` port's animation should be seeked to `0` and reset remain time. This should improve consistency with other nodes when considering oneshot as one kind of transition variation. This is a change in behavior, but since it's a bug fix, so we will add the following brief notice to the release notes along with the breaks compat label: “Since resets now occur correctly, please review your settings to ensure you are not explicitly performing resets.” Here is MRP for testing: [osdemo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23269127/osdemo.zip)

> However, I just realized that there is a bug in the original behavior. So when reset is performed with `Abort on Reset = false`, I think the `shot` port's animation should be seeked to `0` and reset remain time. This should improve consistency with other nodes when considering oneshot as one kind of transition variation.
> 
> This is a change in behavior, but since it's a bug fix, so we will add the following brief notice to the release notes along with the breaks compat label: “Since resets now occur correctly, please review your settings to ensure you are not explicitly performing resets.”

This isn't how it used to be in 4 originally, it regressed at some point. Like I described in my issue, I made all the oneshot-cancelling loops to prevent oneshots from resetting every time, which I noticed sometime during 4.2, when I ported my project from Godot 3. This is something that went unnoticed from ~4.3 to now, since when oneshots started resuming instead of resetting.

> I think false as the default setting is fine.

If the original behavior changing was indeed a bug and not intended like I thought when I wrote the issue, I do think that making true the default setting should be considered, since it is antithetical to the point of using a oneshot that it reset after interruption. That the change that 4.3 brought wasn't noticed until now should be evidence for that, I'd argue that it's worth making a breaking change here.

@TokageItLab would you want to make a bugfix PR for the bug you describe, before this one gets merged? I think the regression may have been caused by #87171, and I don't want to take the wrong approach in solving it. Or should I include it as part of this one?

Got it, makes sense. I'll wait for your PR to get merged then fix conflicts on this one and squash.
Much appreciated, as always.
